2027-02-27.title: Saturday of the Second Week of Lent
readings: You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea
The Lord is kind and merciful
This brother of yours was dead and has come to life
2027-02-27.alt: Lenten weekday. The Alleluia is omitted throughout Lent; the Gloria is omitted except on solemnities and feasts. Liturgical colour: violet. Commemoration of St Gregory of Narek, abbot and Doctor of the Church (its collect may be used).
2027-02-27.verse: So he set off and went to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him.
theo: The prophet Micah ends his book with a prayer and a song of wonder. He asks God to shepherd his people “as in the days of old,” and then breaks out: “Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity and passing over the transgression of the remnant of your possession? He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in showing clemency.” God does not merely tolerate forgiving; he delights in it. “You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.” Sins thrown into the deepest sea are not fished out again. The Psalm adds its own picture: “as far as the east is from the west, so far he removes our transgressions from us.” And it gives us today's refrain: the LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.

Then Jesus tells the parable that has brought more sinners home than perhaps any other page of Scripture. The Pharisees and scribes grumble: “This fellow welcomes sinners and eats with them.” So he tells of a father with two sons. The younger demands his inheritance, as if his father were already dead, and wastes it in a distant country. When famine comes he feeds pigs and longs for their pods. Then “he came to himself” and says: “I will get up and go to my father.” He rehearses a speech, but the father does not let him finish. “While he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him.” Robe, ring, sandals, the fatted calf: the son is restored, not as a hired hand but as a son. Then the elder son, who never left home, refuses to come in. The father goes out to him too: “Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.” The story ends with the question hanging in the air: will he come in? Both sons are lost; both are loved. Today we also remember St Gregory of Narek, the tenth-century Armenian monk and Doctor of the Church, whose Book of Lamentations is a long prayer “speaking with God from the depths of the heart,” the prayer of a sinner who trusts the Father's mercy more than his own sin.
outline: Ask: have you ever been welcomed back when you did not deserve it?
Point 1 · Who is a God like you?
The God who delights in mercy.
He came to himself, and the father ran.
The lost son who never left home.
“This brother of yours was dead and has come to life.”
live: Make your Lenten confession, perhaps this weekend.
If you are the elder brother in some story, take the first step to rejoice with someone who has come back.
2027-02-27.prayer: Father of mercies, you run to meet us while we are still far off. Bring us home from every distant country, cast our sins into the depths of the sea, and free us from the resentment of the elder son. Through the prayers of St Gregory of Narek, teach us to speak with you from the depths of our hearts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The father said: let us eat and celebrate. The Eucharist is the feast the Father prepares for every child who comes home.

quick: God delights in mercy and casts our sins into the depths of the sea.
The father ran to his lost son and restored him as a son.
He went out to the elder son too: both are called to the feast.
2027-02-27.action: Go to confession this weekend, or fix the day for it.
2027-02-27.question: Am I more like the younger son, far from home, or the elder son, near but resentful?

family.explain: A son ran away and wasted all his money. When he came back, sad and hungry, his father ran to him, hugged him and kissed him, and made a big party. God is like that father. He always welcomes us back when we say sorry.
family.intention: We pray for people who are far from God, that they may come home.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family we need to forgive and welcome back?”

illus: A young man from Kollam left home angry and did not call his parents for three years. One Lenten Saturday he took a bus home, rehearsing his apology all the way. When he reached the lane, his mother was already standing at the gate. She said: I have stood here every evening since you left. He never finished his speech.

pm.open: Father of mercies, you run to meet us. Bring us home and teach us to rejoice when others come home. Amen.
share: Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity? (Micah 7:18). Do I believe God delights to forgive me?
I will get up and go to my father (Luke 15:18). What keeps me from going?
Son, you are always with me (Luke 15:31). Do I resent God's mercy to others?
pm.resp: The Lord is kind and merciful.
interc: For those far from home and far from God, that they may come to themselves.
For parents waiting for children who have gone away.
For priests who hear confessions, that they may welcome like the father.
For those who feel resentful and left out, that they may come in to the feast.
For our group, that we may be merciful as the Father is merciful.
pm.close: Father, you rejoice over every child who returns. Make us glad with you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Micah asks in wonder: who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity? He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in showing clemency (Micah 7:18). God does not forgive reluctantly. He delights in it. He casts our sins into the depths of the sea.
Jesus shows us this God in a story. A younger son takes his inheritance and wastes it. When he has nothing left, he comes to himself and says: I will get up and go to my father. He prepares a speech.

But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him (Luke 15:20). The father does not wait. He runs. He does not let the son finish his speech. He gives him a robe, a ring and sandals: you are still my son.

And the elder son, who stayed at home, refuses to come in. The father goes out to him too: son, you are always with me. Today, whether we are the younger son or the elder, the Father is coming out to meet us. St Gregory of Narek prayed: my sins are many, but your mercy is greater (in substance). Let us go home. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told about a boy who ran away and did wrong things. When he came home, his father ran to him and hugged him and had a party! God is like that father. When we say sorry, he runs to hug us.

intro: Theme: “While he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion.”
The God who delights in mercy, the son who came home, and the son who must still come in.

points.h: Who is a God like you?
q: He will again have compassion upon us; he will tread our iniquities under foot. You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
points.apply: Throw one old sin you keep fishing out back into the sea: believe it is forgiven, and stop accusing yourself.

q: as far as the east is from the west, so far he removes our transgressions from us.
So he set off and went to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him.
points.apply: Go to confession before the Third Sunday of Lent if you can.

q: The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.
And the Pharisees and the scribes were grumbling and saying, “This fellow welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
points.apply: Welcome back one person who has returned to the Church or to your family, and rejoice with them.

concl: God delights to forgive, and runs to meet us.
Both sons are invited to the feast; the door is open.
2027-02-27.resolve: Make a good confession this Lent, and forgive as you have been forgiven.
